name: VWA Wednesday Nite Havoc (10/29/95)

date.source: The promotion's own founding post, combining its debut broadcast with its first published rules document.

matches.note: Bret Hart submitted the Terminator with the Sharpshooter to qualify for the promotion's inaugural World Heavyweight tournament.
Derek Holmes submitted Sid Vicious with the Nightmare to qualify for the tournament, in an upset over the much larger Vicious.

The Great Muta pinned Mike Sweetser with a top-rope Frankensteiner to take the tournament's final spot, after Dean Malenko withdrew from the match with a pulled hamstring and placed Muta in his stead.

no_appearances_reason: The show's own undercard also carried a squash match (Ugly Kid Joe over an enhancement wrestler) and a tag-team debut (the Psycho Twins over two enhancement wrestlers); neither is structured here, as none of the enhancement talent involved is named beyond a nickname.
notes: The promotion's debut broadcast, doubling as its own first rules bulletin: three qualifying matches set the final field for its own first pay-per-view a few weeks later.

name: VWA November Nightmare

date.source: The promotion's own three-part broadcast of its first pay-per-view.

matches.note: Mario Ducon advanced to the World Heavyweight tournament final over Bret Hart with what the broadcast itself calls a "cheap shot," managed by Jacques Parizo at ringside.
Marty Jannetty advanced to the tournament final, knocking out Ugly Kid Joe with a chair before a top-rope flying fistdrop.
Mario Ducon won the promotion's inaugural World Heavyweight Championship, pinning Marty Jannetty with the Referendum after Jacques Parizo tripped Jannetty from ringside.
The Steiner Brothers won the promotion's inaugural North American Tag Team Championship, Rick Steiner pinning Booker T with a backslide after Stevie Ray accidentally clotheslined his own partner.
The Travis Brothers won the promotion's inaugural World Tag Team Championship from Demolition in a two-out-of-three-falls match fought under a managers-barred-from-ringside stipulation.

no_appearances_reason: The broadcast's own thirty-two-man over-the-top battle royal for the North American Championship, won by "Demolition Man" Sam Holmes, names every entrant in the ring but is not individually structured as a match; its own text is preserved on the served page.
notes: The promotion's own first pay-per-view: an eight-man tournament crowned its first World Heavyweight Champion, a thirty-two-man battle royal crowned its first North American Champion, and both tag championships changed hands.

name: VWA Survival of the Fittest

date.source: The promotion's own three-part broadcast of its second pay-per-view.

matches.note: Derek Holmes forced "Fantastic" Frank Knight to say "I Quit" with the Nightmare, in a match refereed by the real WWF Champion Bret Hart, who then turned on Holmes afterward, DDTing him and applying the Sharpshooter while Knight added three top-rope legdrops.
The Aerial Marauder beat "Demolition Man" Sam Holmes in a nightstick match, the culmination of a feud running back to the promotion's first pay-per-view.

"Dragon" Kendo Godai won the promotion's World Heavyweight Championship from Marty Jannetty in a one-hour Iron Man match, becoming the first wrestler credited with having held all three of the promotion's singles titles.

no_appearances_reason: The card's own remaining matches (a tag-team ladder match for the North American Tag Team belts, a Thunderdome cage-suspension match, and several undercard bouts) are not individually structured in this pass; their outcomes either do not survive in the read text or fall outside this pass's own selection.
notes: The promotion's own second pay-per-view: eleven stipulated matches by the writer's own account, closing on a title change in the main event and a shocking heel turn by a guest referee.

name: VWA Patriot Games (7/28/1996)

date.source: The promotion's own three-part broadcast of its third pay-per-view, opening with a dedication to the victims of the Centennial Olympic Park bombing the previous night.

matches.note: "The Franchise" Shane Douglas upset Bret Hart, reversing a Wakigatame armbar into a jawbreaker before a belly-to-belly suplex sealed the pin.
The Terminator beat the billed World Wrestling Federation Champion Shawn Michaels with a Death Drop through a table.

A $100,000 ladder match, refereed by special guest Sandman Jr. (not individually structured here): Mill Guest retrieved the suspended prize money first, winning the match and, per its own stipulation, a WCW Television Title shot for RabitHead from Lex Luger.

VWA World Television Championship. Tidal Wave retained against Thunderhawk with the Storm Warning, under a stipulation handcuffing both men's own valets (Slick Rick and Lisa Lightning) together at ringside.
A Calhoun County Street Fight, fought through the arena and its concession stands: Stud Muffin won after an unidentified man knocked RabitHead out with a chair during a figure-four leglock.

A two-out-of-three-falls series decider between Too Many Cooks and the French Connection: Rougeau won the opening fall by roll-up, Danny G evened it with a reverse neckbreaker, and Danny G's Iron Claw forced Pierre-Carl Ouellet to submit for the deciding fall.

A Chicago Street Fight: Law and Order, absent from the promotion for two weeks while hunting Raine Turner and Ugly Kid Joe, arrived to brawl through the arena's front doors and won after a disputed double-referee finish, closing on stereo Swift Justice finishers.
VWA North American Championship. Vader retained against a returning Olympic-silver-medalist challenger, "Whiplash" Barry Williams, with a top-rope moonsault.
VWA World Tag Team Championship. The Midnight Express, managed by Jim Cornette, retained against the former champion Travis Brothers with a variant of the Rock 'n' Roll Express's own Double Goozle.

VWA World Heavyweight Championship, contested under a no-managers, no-countout, no-disqualification stipulation the two lifelong friends agreed between themselves. The Aerial Marauder won the title from Derek Holmes with a rolling cradle, after both men had traded numerous near-falls and visibly bled; the two embraced afterward to a standing ovation.
